newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta call money traded at 9.5/10.0 percent.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta call money traded at 9.5/10.0 percent.

text.p: Jakarta call money was traded at 9.5/10.0 percent on Monday morning on the back of ample rupiah supply, dealers said.
They said an early central bank injection of some 966 billion rupiah seemed to have kept the market in ample supply.
One Japanese bank dealer said the rate did not fall sharply because operators had no alternative financing through the swap market due to a public holiday in the United States.
He said the relatively flush supply was expected to be sustained as tom/next swap rates had declined to 0.32/0.40 points from 0.4/0.5.

However, dealers said short-term liquidity outlook was mixed, as one- and two-week money edged up some 25 basis points from Friday to 12.25 and 12.75 percent, respectively, while one-month money inched down to 13.75 percent.
The average overnight interbank rate on Friday was 9.44 percent, compared with 9.8 percent on Thursday.
